mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, or the average 20-day return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 3.8% signals tight labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppress equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 3.8%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (HOUST) above 1,400,000 units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives higher consumption and corporate earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST > 1,400,000, or the average 60-day return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and deteriorating business conditions, which reduces corporate profitability expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0 for two months, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS signal a persistent inflationary environment that forces the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, increasing equity risk premiums and suppressing forward returns on the S&P 500 over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where both CPIAUCSL > 250.0 and FEDFUNDS > 1.5%, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in interaction regression).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 500,000 million dollars combined with a decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals strong aggregate demand and labor market strength, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 500000 and UNRATE < 4.0%, or the joint signal does not outperform individual proxies in predictive rank IC (IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 250,000 jobs in a single month, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals strong labor demand and rising wage pressures that may trigger inflationary expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 250000 and UNRATE < 4.2%, or the interaction term is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) below 1.5% annualized for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 < 1.5% annualized, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
